title: Comparing Classical and Bayesian VAR Models in Analysing Financial Spillovers: Evidence from Oil, Gold, the U.S. Dollar, and the Thai Stock Market
content: This study examines the dynamic relationships among crude oil, gold, the U.S. Dollar Index, and the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) using daily data from 1 February 2008 to 31 December 2025. Classical VAR and Bayesian VAR models with Minnesota and Normal–Wishart priors are estimated to examine financial spillovers and forecasting performance. Granger causality, impulse responses, FEVD, generalized FEVD, daily out-of-sample forecasts, and regime-based robustness checks are combined. The results show selective and short-lived predictive relationships, while own-market innovations explain about 99% of forecast error variance. Generalized FEVD confirms limited cross-market connectedness, and daily rolling forecasts provide little evidence of predictability beyond a zero-return benchmark. No single VAR or BVAR specification consistently dominates. Regime checks show substantially higher volatility across all four markets during the GFC, particularly high oil volatility during COVID-19, and elevated oil and U.S. dollar volatility during the 2022 Ukraine–commodity shock. Thus, average spillovers are limited, but market risk is heterogeneous across regimes.
